findings.summary: Resolver only queries data-testid/data-test-id, but the scanner also records testid from data-test, so data-test-only elements never resolve.
findings.failure_scenario: scanner.py:113 sets locator.testid from data-testid || data-test-id || data-test. locatorFor suppresses the css fallback whenever testid is truthy. For a form control identified only by data-test with no id and no accessible name (e.g. <input data-test="qty"> with no label/placeholder; accessibleName returns '' for an input), the locator is {testid:'qty', id:null, name:'', css:null}. RESOLVE_JS (service.py:139-140) queries [data-testid="qty"] and [data-test-id="qty"] (no match), skips id (null), skips name (''), skips css (null), and returns {found:false}. The synthesized tool's step for that control then fails at runtime with 'could not find', permanently breaking the tool.

findings.summary: byRelevance selects affordances by live-viewport position when a category exceeds its cap, making the fingerprint scroll-dependent and defeating the cache and verification persistence.
findings.failure_scenario: On a page whose buttons exceed MAX_BUTTONS=25 (the code comment cites reddit.com with 42 buttons), byRelevance ranks by onScreen (r.bottom>0 && r.top<innerHeight) and distance, both viewport-relative, so the selected top-25 set differs with scroll position. Those names feed fingerprint() (store.py:41), so a scan at scroll top yields fingerprint FA and a scan at scroll bottom yields FB != FA. In synthesize() both cache checks miss (in_memory.fingerprint==shape at service.py:476 and store.get(expected_fingerprint=shape) at service.py:479), forcing full re-synthesis every visit; the new tools are verified=False and store.put overwrites the previously-verified manifest. Verification never accumulates across sessions and the disk cache never hits for large pages, defeating the store's stated purpose.

findings.summary: Loose (form-less) controls are scanned and returned as 'controls' but synthesize() never consumes them, so form-less search boxes never become tools.
findings.failure_scenario: The scanner computes loose controls outside any form and returns them under the 'controls' key (scanner.py:255-258,313) with the comment 'a site-wide search box usually lives here.' synthesize() iterates only forms, tables, pagers, toggles, buttons, and views (service.py:488-524) and never reads affordances.get('controls'). A site whose only search is a form-less <input type="search"> wired via JS (common in SPAs / header search boxes not wrapped in <form>) yields no search tool at all, even though the scanner spent budget collecting it; fingerprint() also omits 'controls', confirming it is dead output.

findings.summary: parse_decisions() coerces server-supplied usage token counts with an unguarded int(usage.get(...) or 0), and because it is called on line 95 outside ask()'s try/except, a malformed-but-200 response body makes ask() raise instead of returning an empty Decisions().
findings.failure_scenario: The decision API (or a proxy) returns HTTP 200 with body {"model":"jev-1","usage":{"input_tokens":"n/a"},"answers":{}} (or input_tokens as a non-empty list/dict, e.g. [1]). response.raise_for_status() passes and raw=response.json() succeeds, so control leaves the try/except (which ends at line 93) and reaches `return parse_decisions(raw)` on line 95. Inside parse_decisions, line 125 evaluates int(usage.get('input_tokens') or 0) -> int("n/a") which raises ValueError (or int([1]) -> TypeError for a container). The exception propagates out of parse_decisions -> out of ask(), whose docstring promises 'Never raises' and whose contract is that a bad body 'returns nothing and never raises'. Callers triage_page()/choose_tool() invoke ask() with no try/except, so the exception reaches the agent step, crashing the very code path the module was written to let agents survive. Every other field in parse_decisions is isinstance-guarded (see the answers loop and the confidence/probabilities handling); only these two usage coercions on lines 125-126 assume int-convertibility. Fix: guard both with isinstance(...,(int,float)) or a try/except, matching the rest of the parser.
